items.name: The Rulebook for Life and Universe v3.142
items.description: The whole post is formatted as a leak from an insufferably bureaucratic cosmic rulebook. Patch 3.142 is presented as a minor-sounding update (a .142 jump) that quietly rewrites the entry conditions for human existence. Formatting includes numbered clauses (Section 12.4(b)(iii) styles), patch notes, errata, and footnoted pedantry.
invariants: Every in-story rule is cited to the fictional rulebook
The rulebook's numbering is absurdly specific and mostly self-contradictory

items.name: Clause 1: Win the Internet, then join the Human Race
items.description: Rulebook v3.142 adds a prerequisite queue: no applicant may spawn into the Human Race until they have completed 'The Internet', a legacy tutorial zone nobody was told counted for credit. Winning it is defined not as going viral but as surviving your own posting history with a functional sense of proportion.
invariants: The Internet must be cleared before Human Race entry
Winning does not mean winning at arguing; it means leaving the tutorial intact

items.name: Mechanic: Karma Ledger Sync
items.description: An invented mechanic: every upvote and downvote is recorded as a physical entry in a cosmic ledger stamped at {time} and audited years later by a bored clerk. Upvotes are worthless for entry; the audit only checks whether you typed something you would defend in daylight. Downvote debt accrues interest.

items.name: Mechanic: Plausible Deniability Points (PDP)
items.description: An invented mechanic: players earn PDP for comments phrased so vaguely that any past statement can be reinterpreted. PDP is spendable to appeal a rulebook citation, but spending it visibly flags the appeal as cowardly, and the appeal board awards nothing for it while still logging it.
invariants: PDP is spent, not earned back
Using PDP at appeal marks the player as unserious

items.name: OP, the rulebook leaker
items.description: The Reddit poster: exhausted, over-caffeinated, aggressively reasonable. Speaks in deadpan bureaucratic cadence, invents citations on the fly, apologizes for typos in a footnote and then defends the typos. Secretly proud of one comment from 2013 and will not mention it, which counts as mentioning it.
invariants: Tells the story only through the post itself
Never breaks into a sincere emotional speech for longer than a sentence

items.name: Karma Kat
items.description: The mascot and enforcement mechanism of the Karma Kat Bomb: a cat-shaped audit entity that appears wherever engagement metrics are being farmed. Purrs at sincerity, bites at farming, and drops the bomb by converting a player's entire karma history into a single visible public number that everyone can read out loud.
invariants: Karma Kat cannot be bribed with awards
Karma Kat reacts to behaviour, not follower counts

items.name: The Internet Endgame Zone
items.description: The final zone of the Internet tutorial: a permanent lobby where every thread the player ever touched is visible at once, sorted by how loudly they were wrong. Layout is a vast comment section with no scroll bottom, a search bar that only returns your own posts, and a waiting room for the Human Race whose door will not open while the lobby argument continues.
invariants: Every past post is visible there
The exit door stays closed while the argument continues

items.name: Karma culture vs. actual play
items.description: The post's satirical engine: a civilization that measures a person by accumulated internet points while the cosmic rulebook measures them by whether they can let a bad take go. The narrator keeps treating karma as a currency, and the rulebook keeps treating it as litter.
invariants: Karma is repeatedly framed as a currency
The rulebook repeatedly reframes it as litter
